label: text
text: PIRATE CHIEF'S SWANK.

label: text
text: Dead Men's Heads Instead of

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Pukkai, Kongmoon, June 10.

label: text
text: Three dead men's heads were laid on the table at a dinner, for decoration instead of flowers, when Leung She (the notorious bandit chief) invited some "colleagues" to dinner to discuss business.

label: text
text: I do not know whether this novel item suitably impressed the guests or not but Leung. She needs no advertisement of this sort.

label: text
text: Banditry has now been put on a systematic footing.

label: text
text: Neighbouring communities have devised schemes for mutual protection, including the lighting of bonfires to warn the countryside, signals, etc., whereby one village helps the other in repalling piractical attacks. Forts and towers have been put up to serve as crow's-nests.

label: text
text: In view of expected resistance, the pirates have banded themselves together so as to be strong enough to overcome opposition. At Nam Po, in the Sanwui "district, several outlaw chieftains met and devised the following system:—

label: text
text: A band of 100 strong or over, to take three shares of the loot; 60 strong to count for, two shares; 30 strong, one share.

label: paragraph_title
text: Pay—Or Death.

label: text
text: Two more victims were put to death at Lai Ngok by a gang whose leader is known as Chau Sui. The bodies were thrown into the river. Two more are reported from Kowkong.

label: text
text: Two “prisoners,” whose relatives had failed to pay ransom for, were shot in cold blood by pirates, early in the morning at Ko Sha, 300 yards from the busy railway station at Pakkali.

label: text
text: The Naval Department has ordered twelve gunboats to patrol the waterways, which will be divided into sections, as though they were miniature naval stations. Various strategic points on the West and East rivers will be regularly patrolled.

label: text
text: From the United States, a telegram from Chinese residents has been sent back asking for the stamping out of piracy in the (four) Sze Yap districts. (Note: The majority of Chinese emigrants in America are from the Sze Yap).

label: text
text: Kwong "Hoi city is suffering from a shortage of food. Shops are closed and things are at a standstill because of the proximity of pirates.

label: paragraph_title
text: BLIND EVANGELIST.

label: paragraph_title
text:
ELLIS ISLAND OFFICIALS
PUZZLED.

label: text
text: N QUARANTINE

label: text
text: (Router's American Service.)

label: text
text: The Ellis Island officials are puzzled to know what to do with the well-known Scottish blind evangelist, Neil McIntyre, who arrived from Glasgow to conduct a revivalist campaign in the Southern States and was detained in quarantine because nobody came to meet him.

label: text
text: New York, June 14.

label: text
text: A special Board inquired into the case and decided that McIntyre must stay on the island until & guarantees was forthcoming that he would not become a charge on the American public!

label: paragraph_title
text: WEATHER FORECAST.

label: text
text: For the 24 hours ending at noon to-morrow, the weather forecast is East winds, fresh to moderate; generally cloudy, some rain.

label: text
text: A Chinese girl was sent to hospital yesterday suffering from slight injuries as a result of walking in front of a tram car at Connaught Road West.

label: text
text: On a charge of possession of an automatic pistol and 85 rounds of ammunition, which was not pressed by the police, an assistant bosun on the s.a. "Derwent" was fined $75 at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning.

text: BRITISH WARNING.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: London, June 14

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, in reply to a number of questions on the subject of British-Russian relations and alleged Soviet activities in Great Britain, Sir Austen Chamberlain, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, replied that in the negotiations with the late Charge d'Affaires he had been content generally to state the policy of His Majesty's Government respecting anti-British propaganda. He did not consider that any useful purpose would be served by detailed protests against particular incidents, but a few days ago—before leaving for Geneva—had instructed "His Majesty's Charge d'Affaires in Moscow to inform the Soviet that it was impossible for His Majesty's Government to ignore the action of the Soviet Commissariat of Finance in specially authorising the transfer to Great Britain of funds destined to support an illegal and unconstitutional general strike — (Conservative cheers)—as not conducting to a friendly settlement of outstanding questions which the Soviet Government had professed to desire.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: (British Wireless Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: Necessary Conditions for Negotiations.

label: text
text: Ruzby, Junê 14.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain replied in the House of Commons to a series of questions respecting the money sent from Russia to this country.

label: text
text: He said that in the conversations which he had had from time to time with the late Russian Charged Affairs he had clearly stated that anti-British propaganda here and elsewhere was one of the main obstacles to any improvement in British-Russian relations as long as it continued. The British Government had always felt that the necessary conditions of successful negotiations were: Firstly—Ac

text:

He had sought in the main to state that policy of His Majesty's Government in its general terms and had not considered that any useful purpose would be served by detailed protests in regard to particular instances.
A few days ago, however, just before he left for Geneva, he had instructed the British Charged Affairs in Moscow to inform the Soviet Government that His Majesty's Government could not page-over-in-silence-the-action-of the Commissariat of Finance in giving special authorisation for the transfer to this country of funds destined for support of the general strike. The Charge d'Affaires was to point out that the general strike was an illegal and unconstitutional act and one constituting a serious threat to established order; and that the special action taken by the Soviet Commissariat of Finance in its favour did not conduce to the friendly settlement which the Soviet Government professed to desire.

label: text
text:

Sir Austen Chamberlain replied: What is within our knowledge and was the ground of my protest is that the stipulations of the law in force have been waived in order to permit the transmission, of this money in support of an illegal and unconstitutional strike.

label: paragraph_title
text: SUPREME COURT.

label: text
text: NO GROUNDS FOR CREDITOR'S ALLEGATIONS.

label: text
text: THE WO ON COMPANY.

label: text
text: " Allegations made at the last Bankruptcy Court were referred to at the Supreme Court this

label: text
text: to at the Supreme Court this morning, His Lordship sitting in bankruptcy jurisdiction for a few minutes to deal with the case which referred to the affairs of the We On Company.

label: text
text: At the last court it was stated on behalf of one of the creditors that the trustee whom other creditors had mentioned in connection with the bankruptcy, also other proposed members of a committee of inspection were partners in the firm.

label: text
text: This morning, Mr. D. W. Trattman, Official Receiver, said that he had investigated the allegations and found that the creditor in question had no real grounds for complaint and, no evidence whatever on which to base his statement. He therefore asked that an order be made in terms of his original application.

label: text
text: His Lordship asked if Mr. J. T. Prior, who represented the creditor, had anything to say and Mr. Prior replied that he had no alternative to offer.

label: text
text: An order for adjudication, appointment of trustee and committee was therefore made.

label: paragraph_title
text: Other Cases:

label: text
text: Permission to file allotments out of date was applied for by Mr. H. S. Fitzroy, the shares in question being those of the Hip Fat Company.

label: text
text: Counsel stated that a firm of brokerage and forwarding agents was originally in existence and a private company was formed in January, 1925. The latter had a nominal capital of $20,000 divided into 400 shares of $50 each.

label: text
text: Ten of these shares were paid in respect of the goodwill of the old firm, stated counsel, the remainder being provided in cash. There were only two in the Company, father and son, and of the remaining 390 shares, 385 went to the father and 5 to the son.

text: Failure to file returns was due to inadvertence

label: text
text: Affidavits in connection with the affairs of the National, Commercial and Savings Bank, Ltd., having been filed, His Lordship granted an extension of time to file registration of certain mortgages which had been entered into by the Shanghai branch but which concerned property in Hongkong.

label: text
text: This was an adjourned case from yesterday, Mr. H. G. Sheldon making the application.

label: text

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON.. DOINGS.

label: paragraph_title
text: MASS CELEBRATIONS ON

label: text
text: LATEST RUMOURS.

label: text
text: Over a hundred organisations were represented at a mass celebration in Canton yesterday, the sponsors being the combined Association representing merchants, labourers, schools, etc.

label: text
text: This Association is the one that submitted a series of resolutions to the Canton Government asking for the boycott to be ended.

label: text
text: Although Hongkong. Chinese merchants were not represented in any considerable numbers, the feeling was that there was not enough time to bring up many in time for the festival.

label: text
text: From a semi-official source in Canton it is gathered that a suggestion may be put forward—as one of the considerations for the projected peace conference—that a tax be levied on persons going in and out of Canton, from Hongkong, in the shape of a fairly substantial passport fee — one payment to hold good for continual use. This suggestion, it is stated, is being discussed by the merchants.

text: DECISION ON THE LEAGUE COUNCIL.

label: text
text: MINISTER'S DISCRETION.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Madrid, Juné 14.

label: text
text:
The Cabinet has decided not to present Spain's candidature for a non-permanent seat on the League Council.
It has also empowered the Foreign Minister to act as circumstances dictate at Geneva:

label: paragraph_title
text: Geneva, June 14.

label: text
text: The Secretary-General of the League of Nations has received a telegram from the Brazilian Foreign Ministry conveying the decision of the Brazilian Government to cease membership of the League of Nations, in accordance with article one of the Covenant, adding that Brazil will not participate in the meeting of the Assembly of the League in September.

label: paragraph_title
text:
SOVIET FRONTIER GUARD'S
MISTAKE.

label: text
text: NO DAMAGE DONE

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: 'Warsaw' June 14.

label: text
text: When^ Pelletier D'Olsy, the French airman, was crossing the Poland-Soviet frontier for Moscow a Soviet frontier-guard fired-on-his aeroplane, presumably mistaking it for a Polish one.

label: text
text: No damage was done, and D'Oisy rapidly ascended out of range.

label: paragraph_title
text: SIR H. MORRIS.

label: text
text: DEATH OF WELL-KNOWN SURGEON.

label: text
text: A GREAT REPUTATION

label: text
text: (British Wireless Service.)

label: text
text: Rugby, June 14.

label: text
text: The death is announced of Sir Henry Morris, the well-known surgeon and one of the founders of the Imperial Research Fund. So great was his reputation as a surgeon, especially for operations on the kidneys, that in 1904 he was summoned on a professional visit to Bombay—at that time the only European Surgeon who had ever been called to India to operate.

label: paragraph_title
text: MAIL ARRIVAL

label: text
text:
A heavy mail, comprising 688 bags from Canada the U.S.A., Japan and Shanghai, arrived this afternoon and will be ready for delivery later in the day.
Included in the total were two bags via Siberia and 10 bags via Canada from Europe.

label: paragraph_title
text: POLICE COURT ITEMS.

label: text
text: HARBOUR CHASE RESULT.

label: text
text: A Chinese detective from Shaukiwan gave evidence before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning of a chase in the harbour and the arrest of three men on a dinghy on Sunday night. Nothing incriminating was found on the men when they were eventually stopped, but they were charged with unlawful possession of the boat.

label: text
text: On explanations being offered by two of the men, all the defendants were discharged, but the third who had remained silent was charged in another case for returning to the Colony while serving an order of banishment. His explanation was that he could not help coming here, as he was working on a fishing junk. He was sentenced to nine months hard labour and 15 strokes of the birch.

label: paragraph_title
text: Unwholesome Food.

label: text
text: At 7.30 this morning a Chinese was caught on the praya in the act of cutting up a pig. Examination of the carcase by the Veterinary Surgeon showed that the animal had been dead a few hours, and the man was subsequently charged for preparing an unslaughtered pig for sale as food.

label: text
text: Defendant explained that he was cutting up the pig to extract the fat out of it and not with the intention of selling the meat. He was fined $10, or fourteen days.

label: text
text: Major C. Willson delivered sentence to-day in the case of a Chinese who was found guilty yesterday on a number of charges of theft, and pawning stolen goods, these including a gold watch and chain taken from the room of Mr. Kelly Sayce. He was given a total of twelve months' hard labour.

label: text
text: Claiming to be of Swedish nationality but an "American citizen," John Olson, a seaman, pleaded to be without money or work in an awer to a charge of being a vagrant.

label: text
text:
Sub-Inspector Wutt said he believed the man had been in Court before. He was always missing his ship and had been refused admittance at the Sailors' Home.
A committal was made to the House of Detention.

label: text
text:
Traffic Breaches.
A case in which Mr. R. F. Lindsell (the senior Magistrate) was the complainant was heard among others. by Major Willson. A Chinese lorry driver was charged with attempting "to overtake another vehicle on a bend at Stubb Road while the complainant was coming down the road with his car. He was fined $25.

label: text
text: On each of two charges of failing to notify his change of address and causing obstruction with his car, Mr. G. A. Hyder was fined $5.

label: text
text: In a case at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning, a Chinese woman had to go through a ceremony of burning joss paper and cutting a fowl in the temple in order to establish her claim to three pigs.

label: text
text:
A Chinese, charged with the "car-
ceny of the animals, claimed that
he bought them. Mr. Leo
d'Almada, defending, brought out
the fact that a suggestion had been
made to the woman to establish
her claim by going through a temple
ceremony.

label: text
text: The complainant thought this was unnecessary, as she was sure the animals belonged to her. The Magistrate (Mr. Nihill) remarked that all pigs were alike. She eventually agreed to carry out the ceremony, and this being done, she carried away her pigs.
